cells.tense: You are standing at the turning, and you can feel what is arriving come in.
cells.act: close the cycle and leave the door open for the next
cells.ask: Find the piece that's nearly finished, and finish it. Complete, not sealed off — leave a way back in without keeping it open as an excuse to stall.
cells.core:
You can tell the difference between arriving and having arrived. Something shows up at your edge — an offer, a person, a shift in what you want — and you take it in rather than brace against it. The light you steer by stays real because you keep choosing it in plain moments, not because you found a formula.

What's ready to close, close. Not shut — finished, with the next thing free to start. There is a point where the cycle has done its work, and you recognise it without needing it to feel like an ending. Finish the nearly-done piece, and leave the way open for whatever arrives next. That is not the end of the pattern; it's what lets the next thing in.
cells.sheetLine: You meet what arrives, and you know when a cycle is complete.
cells.verb: meeting what arrives at the turning and letting it enter whole
cells.place: where the pull toward what you actually want is felt — the draw toward a light you steer by

cells.tense: You are already living past the next thing, before it has shown you anything.
cells.act: complete it without making it final
cells.ask: Choose something you've been carrying as unfinished. Do the last small step you can actually do, and stop. Don't add a second ending to make it feel safer.
cells.core:
You keep moving with a current instead of meeting it at the edge, and the current runs ahead of you. The next version of your life has already played out in your mind, so what's actually here feels too slow, too plain. The name you give it is timing, or fate, or just how things are going; the patterns repeat and you're already past them.

One thing can still be completed — not closed for good, only the last step done. Finish that step and stop there. Don't build the next chapter over it to make it feel safe. What you finish stays finished without being shut, and the current you've been riding slows down enough that you can meet it where it is.

cells.verb: meeting what arrives at the turning and letting it enter whole
cells.place: where the pull toward what you actually want is felt — the draw toward a light you steer by

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that closed behind you, waiting to be let through.
cells.act: let the finished thing be the start of something
cells.ask: Take a role, a room, a way of being that has already ended — do the single next thing that only makes sense because it's over. Not a resolve. An action.
cells.core:
You have been naming this stillness, or non-attachment, or keeping your peace. But nothing is arriving for you to meet, because you are not standing where things arrive. The light you steer by got moved out of reach, and waiting for the right state now fills the whole stance.

Start smaller than that. Find one thing that already finished, and do the single next action that only makes sense because it's done — a call no longer owed, a shelf cleared, a routine that assumed the old thing. It doesn't have to mean anything. It just has to be an action taken because the old thing is over. The pull comes back through finishing — not the other way around.

cells.tense: You are writing on the page without knowing the pen is in your hand.
cells.act: set a direction and take the first step in it
cells.ask: Pick a direction — not the best one, one you can name — and take the first small step toward it. Put the choice somewhere you'll see it, out of mind.
cells.core:
Things keep happening to you that you didn't see coming, and each time you are surprised. The patterns cycle and you report them like a forecast. Somebody else must be running this, or nobody is, and either way you are not the one choosing — so the pull toward what you want stays in the background, unnamed.

Pick a direction, even a rough one. Set the choice where your eye will find it again, and take the smallest step today that moves toward it. Where it ends isn't known in advance; what matters is saying yes to a thing and acting on it. The surprise fades the moment the pen is back in your hand.
cells.sheetLine: You are moving without knowing you are the one moving.
cells.verb: meeting what arrives at the turning and letting it enter whole

attempts.check: The one claim the record does not support is that the person can tell 'each moment is fresh entry' as a felt state — Balanced's face is recognition, not a feeling, so the core stays with what they can notice doing, not what they feel. A reader could say the Balanced cell sounds like it's asking them to journal about arrival, which the record's medicine (Creation: completion) does not say; the ask must stay on closing the cycle, not on reflection. The Too Little ask risks reading as 'practice being present,' which the vertical rule explicitly forbids — the act must be the medicine's own (completion), and I've written it so. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is the Too Much sheetLine's 'fate replaces choice' phrasing; it is not said on glass. If my read is wrong, each ask still teaches something: closing a thing, letting a finished thing seed the next, each is true of any life where something is nearly done.
